prompt: Use BiFunction for two classic two-argument jobs: fold walks a list carrying an accumulator, and zip pairs two lists element by element and stops at the shorter one.
explanation: BiFunction<A, B, R> is the two-argument member of the function family, and its three type parameters are what let fold carry an accumulator of a different type from the items -- summing string lengths turns Strings into an Integer total. fold is the shape behind Stream.reduce: seed, then one apply per element, each result feeding the next. zip needs no accumulator, only the smaller of the two sizes, which is the whole edge case: reading past the end of the shorter list would throw.
hints: fold keeps a local of type A initialised to seed, then reassigns it to step.apply(accumulator, item) for each item.
Math.min(left.size(), right.size()) gives zip its loop bound.
Both methods build their result with an ordinary loop -- the BiFunction is called once per element, never stored.
